interpretations.rationale: The account of this question stands on one fully-resolved receipt for both completion paths of one accepted request. Source side: a leader postpones MsgReadIndex exactly when its configuration is not a singleton and no entry of its term is committed (raft.go:1354-1372); the only code that discharges the duty is releasePendingReadIndexMessages, called from the MsgAppResp commit path alone (raft.go:1550-1554), although switchToConfig also performs the term's first commit (raft.go:2013-2028) and the helper is guarded only by committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (raft.go:2127-2145); a postponed request is absent from readOnly.unconfirmedReads, so no heartbeat carries its context (read_only.go:93-101, raft.go:1600-1602). Receipt a1859bb05261498c820729722eef035f (24 events, no parse loss, ten comparisons all resolved). Local path, removal of the unreachable voter 4: the request is postponed (parsed index 2, stashed true, committed_entry_term 1 against leader_term 2); applying the committed change advances committed 10 -> 11 with committed_entry_term 2 equal to leader_term, i.e. the release condition the helper is guarded by becomes true, yet pending_reads stays 1 with read_states 0 (index 3 - the violated witness); the delayed acknowledgement of the old configuration (index 4) and a heartbeat round with an empty read context (index 5, violated: no ReadState) do not repair it; only the unrelated proposal committed through the MsgAppResp path releases it (index 6, holds: ctx A, read index 12). Variant in the same receipt: applying the committed zero change leaves the joint configuration and the incoming half performs the same first commit, with the request still pending (index 11, violated) and released only by the unrelated proposal (index 14, holds). Forwarded path: follower 2 forwards the client's request to the leader it knows (index 18, holds: StateFollower emitting MsgReadIndex), the leader postpones it (index 19, holds: pending_reads 1, node2_read_states 0), applying the committed change again performs the first commit of the term with no MsgReadIndexResp emitted and follower 2 without a ReadState (index 20, violated), and only the unrelated proposal produces the response (index 23, holds: one MsgReadIndexResp, node2_read_states 1, ctx A, index 12). The defect statement is therefore: a ReadIndex request that a leader accepts by postponing can remain unanswered across a commit of an entry of its own term when switchToConfig performs that commit, for both consumers of the answer (a local ReadState and a forwarded MsgReadIndexResp), and no periodic or acknowledgement path inside raft repairs it; the answer, when it eventually arrives after an unrelated commit or a client retry, carries an index that is still safe because it is taken from raftLog.committed at release time and the commit index never decreases - the failure is an unfulfilled duty, not a wrong index.

knowledge.assertion: A leader postpones MsgReadIndex exactly when the configuration is not a singleton and committedEntryInCurrentTerm() is false.
Postponed requests are released only from the MsgAppResp commit path.
switchToConfig can perform the term's first commit and does not release pendingReadIndexMessages.
A postponed request is not in readOnly.unconfirmedReads, so heartbeats cannot release it.
The applied progress report and the ApplyConfChange call are not ordered by the library's contract.

counterevidence: The controls hold in this receipt (parsed indices 6, 14 and 23): an unrelated proposal committed through the MsgAppResp path releases the postponed request and the answer is delivered (ctx A, index 12), so the release mechanism is intact and the omission is specific to the switchToConfig commit path.

The Node.ReadIndex contract tells callers that read index requests can be lost without notice and that retries are their duty (node.go:218-224), so a retrying client is not blocked; the observation is an unanswered admissible request rather than a permanent client-visible outage.

The reachable prefix relies on documented application latitude: an application may report applied progress before it finishes applying the entries of a previous Ready (node.go:166-178) and the library fixes no ordering between that report and the required ApplyConfChange call for a change it has observed (node.go:179-187); the unanswered request is not caused by that latitude, only the reachability of the state is.
limitations: The comparison holds the applied configuration change to be the one that first makes a current-term entry committable; a leader that had already committed any entry of its term answers later requests normally (committedEntryInCurrentTerm() is true, so nothing is postponed).

The retained harness supplies the starting log, HardState and applied index as an application state fixture (ten term-1 entries with entry 10 the configuration change, persisted commit 10, applied 10) while the election, the acknowledgements, the read requests, the applied change and the proposal are driven through real raft messages; voter 4 is unreachable and voter 3's append acknowledgements are delayed.

No state machine was run, so the consequence measured is the unanswered request itself (no ReadState, no MsgReadIndexResp). The safe-but-late index of the eventual answer follows from the contract, not from a served value in the receipt.

The state's reachability without the documented application latitude, and any consequence of the unreleased request beyond the unanswered caller (for example under a lease-based read configuration), remain unmeasured.
interpretations.joint_history: This receipt is the third basis of the same harness family: same four-voter group, same bootstrap fixture (ten term-1 entries with entry 10 the configuration change, persisted commit 10, applied 10), same transport fault model (voter 4 unreachable, voter 3's append acknowledgements delayed) and the same decisive interval (elect node 1, deliver the read, apply the committed change, observe the release, then observe the unrelated commit). Its event stream contains the two original cases in their original order (indices 2-6 and 11-14) plus the forwarded case (indices 18-23), and the forwarded events are now emitted with distinct fwd_-prefixed names, which is why every comparison resolves here while four of them were unknown in the earlier forwarded basis (f6f942daf8df40abb36626675d6923fb). The decisive indices therefore carry the same meaning as in receipt 5d77b839c94544d1bf81b71c506a5b90.
